courseName: IB Environmental Systems and Societies HL
practicesLabel: Inquiry, Systems Thinking and HL Extensions
practices: Assessments evaluate core environmental concepts plus all HL Extensions. High emphasis on advanced systems modeling, environmental economics, and international policy analysis. Strict adherence to command terms.

units.unitTitle: Foundations of environmental systems and societies (SL + HL)
keyTopics: Environmental value systems (EVS): ecocentric, anthropocentric, technocentric
Systems and models: open, closed, isolated systems
Energy and equilibria: laws of thermodynamics, stability
Sustainability, ecological footprint
Environmental economics and ethics (HL Extension)
Species and populations, carrying capacity, population dynamics and modeling (HL Extension)
Communities and ecosystems, interactions (competition, predation)
Flows of energy and matter, food chains, pyramids
Biomes, zonation and ecological succession
An introduction to biodiversity: genetic, species, habitat
Origins of biodiversity, natural selection, plate tectonics
Threats to biodiversity, species extinction, red list
Conservation of biodiversity, reserves, treaties

units.unitTitle: Water and aquatic food production systems
keyTopics: Water systems and resources, hydrological cycle
Access to fresh water, water conservation
Aquatic food production systems, fisheries
Water pollution, eutrophication

units.unitTitle: Soil systems and terrestrial food production (SL + HL)
keyTopics: Introduction to soil systems, soil profile, horizons
Terrestrial food production systems and food choices
Soil degradation and conservation strategies
Global environmental policies and geopolitics (HL Extension)

examFormat.freeResponse: Paper 2: Short-answer and structured essays (70%), 2 hours

antiPatterns: Ensure students show advanced policy evaluation and systems modeling. Out of scope are: memorization of local/regional legislation details beyond standard international treaties (CITES, Montreal Protocol, Kyoto Protocol); and speculative ecological theories not supported by standard environmental models.
